messages:
alex.chen: Customer on Private deployment reporting intermittent 503s; Canary ALB target group health checks flip from healthy->unhealthy every few minutes. They say app is fine and only health checks fail. Hoping for quick triage.

maria: Which LB type and health check protocol? ALB vs NLB and HTTP vs HTTPS matters a lot.

alex.chen: Internal ALB, target group uses HTTPS health checks on /healthz:8443. Target is an envoy sidecar on ecs/ec2 (customer-managed). Health check logs show TLS handshake timeout. No obvious app errors.

samir: Can you paste the target's envoy logs around the handshake timeout? Also, any tcpdump or curl from inside the same subnet?

alex.chen: Pasting relevant excerpts: `2026-02-18T09:12:03Z envoy tls error: handshake timeout waiting for client hello` then `2026-02-18T09:12:03Z http health check failed status 0 -> mark unhealthy`

maria: Two likely classes: 1) network (SG / route / egress) where LB probes never reach target, leading to timeouts OR 2) TLS side (SNI/Host mismatch) where ALB probe doesn't send SNI so server aborts. We had a case where customers had TLS certificates selected by SNI and probes used IP -> no SNI -> handshake failed.

karen: Also check internal DNS: if their health check uses hostname (ALB config can set Host header) but targets resolve differently inside VPC, there can be mismatch. Does the ALB use Host override or default (IP)?

alex.chen: ALB config uses default (no Host override). Health check connects to target IP and port. Customer said their server requires SNI to pick the right cert (multitenant).

samir: Quick repro steps I recommend customer run from a host in the same subnet as the target (or from the target itself) to emulate LB probe:
```
# from bastion in same AZ
curl -vk --resolve internal.app.example:8443:10.0.5.12 https://internal.app.example:8443/healthz
# Or test with IP and custom Host header:
curl -vk -H 'Host: internal.app.example' https://10.0.5.12:8443/healthz
```

maria: Note: using raw IP + Host header DOES send SNI in modern curl builds only if you pass --resolve or use hostname in URL. --resolve guarantees SNI matches Host. If curl to IP and Host header might not set SNI. Good to show both.

alex.chen: Customer ran `curl -vk https://10.0.5.12:8443/healthz` and saw `* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1)` then `* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, fatal: handshake failure` — ambiguous. They also ran tcpdump: `sudo tcpdump -n -s0 -A host 10.0.5.12 and port 8443` --> shows client_hello packets without SNI extension.

karen: That points strongly at SNI being absent. ALB HTTPS health checks do NOT set the SNI host header to the host header you might expect in every case. And internal targets that rely on SNI-based cert selection will reject. Workarounds:
- Configure the target to present a default cert that matches the IP/health-check host, OR
- Use HTTP health checks if possible (no TLS) on a dedicated health endpoint, OR
- Configure ALB to use an explicit Host header that matches cert (ALB supports Host override on target group health checks?) Check console.

samir: Another angle: network egress/DNS. If target tries to validate client or call back to auth endpoint during health check (some apps do) and the VPC egress rule blocks outbound DNS or outbound 443, the handshake can still stall. Confirm security groups and NACLs allow ephemeral replies and allow ALB SG as source. Also confirm there is no egress allowlist blocking outbound 53/443 to your org's resolver.

alex.chen: Customer also uses custom VPC-based DNS resolver (inbound resolver endpoints). We found their VPC resolver policy forwards certain domains to a firewall appliance that occasionally drops packets when under load. Could explain intermittent flapping.

maria: Actionable triage checklist to share with customer (short):
- tcpdump on target during a failing health check: `sudo tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/hc.pcap host <ALB-node-ip> and port 8443` (capture both directions)
- Confirm SNI present in ClientHello: `tshark -r /tmp/hc.pcap -Y 'tls.handshake.extensions_server_name' -V` or `tshark -r /tmp/hc.pcap -T fields -e tls.handshake.extensions_server_name`
- Test with curl using `--resolve` to emulate SNI: `curl -vk --resolve internal.app.example:8443:10.0.5.12 https://internal.app.example:8443/healthz`
- Check target SG inbound rules include ALB security group (not just IPs) and allow ephemeral ports: `aws ec2 describe-security-groups --group-ids <sg>`
- Check VPC route table & NACLs for asymmetric routing/NAT that could drop return packets
- If using an internal DNS forwarder, verify its logs and that it can resolve quickly under load

karen: If SNI is confirmed missing we should ask the customer to either: add a default cert on envoy that covers health check host OR change health check to HTTP. If they need TLS for health checks, they must ensure the probe SNI matches a cert on the server (ALB behavior varies; sometimes you need to set Host header in health check config).

alex.chen: I pushed the checklist and tcpdump commands to the customer. They came back with results: tcpdump shows ClientHello without server_name extension about ~20% of the attempts, and their DNS forwarder logs show short-lived errors that align with the failures. So dual root cause: intermittent DNS resolver overload + SNI-dependent cert selection.

samir: Nice catch on the dual failure. Short-term mitigation: switch target group health protocol to HTTP on a health-only port or add a permissive default cert. Long-term: fix the resolver appliance or move to Route53 resolver endpoints + scale.

alex.chen: Customer implemented an HTTP-only health endpoint on 8080 and ALB target group health checks switched to HTTP -> health stabilized. They'll follow up to rotate certs/add default cert and fix DNS.

infra-bot: deploy-check: target-group/rg-12 switched health-check-protocol from HTTPS->HTTP at 2026-02-18T10:02:15Z by support. (automated note)

deploy-bot: ticket#INC-1249 updated: root cause recorded as "SNI-required server + intermittent DNS resolver failures causing ALB HTTPS health check TLS handshake timeouts". Assigned to customer infra to remediate DNS; support will mark resolved after one day of stable checks. :white_check_mark:
